name: com.meetkatalis/katalis
title: Katalis UK company checks
description: UK company checks: Companies House, payments, contracts, registers. No key: 19 tools; free key: 56

tools.name: company_search
tools.description: Search UK registered companies. Companies House search, cleaned and confidence-ranked (company-level only, never officer personal data). Use this first when you have only a name, or a name could mean several companies, then pass the chosen company number to the other tools. Companies only, never people.

q.description: A company name or part of one, a former name, or a company number.

limit.description: Max results (1-50, default 10), best match first.

tools.name: public_record
tools.description: Everything the public record says about a UK company, joined and read. Registry facts, distress signals, directors' and PSCs' ID verification against the deadline, and (for large companies) the payment-practices record, with the three things most worth knowing first. Also public contracts won, the gender pay gap, Environment Agency registrations and a UK Sanctions List check. 3 credits. One call that joins several of the other tools for a first look; for one register in full use its own tool (accounts, charges, ownership, registers, contracts_won).

company.description: A company number, or a name (resolved to one company, named in the reply)

tools.name: ownership
tools.description: Who controls the company, followed up the register. The people-with-significant-control chain followed company by company while the controller is a UK-registered company (up to five levels) - each company's name, number, status and insolvency flag, what each controller holds, where the register ends (a foreign parent, a listed company, a PSC statement), and any trouble above. Individuals counted, never named. 2 credits. Use this for who controls the company up the chain of parent companies; for directors' and PSCs' ID verification use idv_check (key needed).

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: accounts
tools.description: The company's latest filed accounts read into plain figures, this year and last. From Companies House's tagged (iXBRL) accounts document - net assets, current assets, cash, debtors, creditors due within and after a year, equity, turnover and profit where the accounts include them, average employees, for the current and prior period; audit status, standards, dormant flag; what the accounts leave out. Accounts filed as a PDF can't be read and the call's credits go back. 2 credits. Use this for the figures themselves; for whether accounts are due or overdue use deadlines, for the company's health distress_signals.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: ppn_018
tools.description: A company's statutory payment reports against the PPN 018 tests and the Fair Payment Code tiers. The last two Payment Practices reports read against PPN 018's tests (at least 95% of invoices paid within 60 days, 90% with an action plan; all invoices paid within an average of 45 days) and the Fair Payment Code's percentage tiers (Gold 95% within 30 days; Bronze 95% within 60; Silver can't be judged from the report). A company that doesn't report is said so. 1 credit. Use this for public-procurement payment tests; for the plain record use payment_practices, for the cost on your invoice will_they_pay.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: charges
tools.description: A company's registered charges in plain English. From the Companies House register of charges - total and outstanding, the lenders (individuals never named), what each secures and over what, fixed or floating, a floating charge over everything, and the latest creation date. 1 credit. Use this for who has lent against the company and over what; for the company's health use distress_signals, for a first look across the record public_record.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: aml_register
tools.description: Is a business on HMRC's Money Laundering Regulations supervised business register, for what, and since when. Matched on the business's name as the register writes it (a company number brings its registered and former names), with the register's postcode district checked against the registered office. Current registrations with sectors and status (Approved, Applied, Expired), former ones with the date they went, and every change recorded for the name since 7 October 2026. HMRC is one supervisor among several, so absence never means unsupervised. People never loaded. 1 credit. Use this for HMRC's register only; a business supervised by a professional body (law firms, most accountants) is on that body's register instead, and for law firms use sra_check.

company.description: A company number, or the business's name

tools.name: charity_check
tools.description: Is this a registered charity, is it in good standing, and what do its accounts say. Read live from the Charity Commission for England and Wales' register, by charity number, by company number (matched through the Companies House number the register holds) or by name (up to three matches, registered first). Registered or removed with dates and reason; CIO or charitable company; insolvency, administration and interim-manager flags; reporting status; latest accounts and up to six years of income and spend broken down; what it does, for whom and where; trustee count and chair; governing document, objects, other regulators. England and Wales only. Trustees counted, never named. Contains information from the Charity Commission, Open Government Licence v3.0. 1 credit. Use this for charities in England and Wales; for a charity's annual report read in full use charity_report (key needed).

company.description: A charity number (263710, or 1053467-2 for a group member), a company number, or a charity's name

tools.name: cqc_check
tools.description: Is this company a CQC-registered care provider, how are its services rated, and has that changed. Matched on our daily copy of the Care Quality Commission's register of providers (the CQC's own Companies House number, then the company's registered and former names, or a CQC provider or location id); the provider and up to twelve of its registered locations are then read live from the CQC. Registered or deregistered with dates; the kind of provider; every location (care homes, agencies, surgeries, clinics) with its overall rating, the five key questions, inspection and report dates; every change recorded for it since 2 October 2026. England only. Organisations and services only, never people. Contains CQC information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. 1 credit. Use this for health and adult social care providers in England; for an inspection report read in full use cqc_report (key needed).

company.description: A company number, a provider's name, or a CQC provider or location id (1-…)

tools.name: sra_check
tools.description: Is this an SRA-authorised law firm, what kind, since when, and has that changed. From our daily copy of the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register of regulated organisations. Matched on the register's own Companies House number, then the company's registered and former names, or by SRA number. Authorised, authorised with conditions, ceased, revoked or intervened, with dates; the kind of firm; work areas, offices and head office; trading and former names; every change recorded for the firm since 8 October 2026. Firms only, never individuals. Data supplied by the Solicitors Regulation Authority. 1 credit. Use this for law firms in England and Wales; for HMRC's anti-money-laundering register use aml_register.

company.description: A company number, a firm's name, or an SRA number

tools.name: late_payment
tools.description: Statutory interest and fixed compensation on a late business invoice. Under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, interest at 8% over the Bank Rate on the previous 30 June or 31 December (each half-year at its own rate), simple, by the day, from the day after the due date to the paid date (today if unpaid), plus the fixed compensation (£40 / £70 / £100 by the invoice's size). The Bank Rate is read from the Bank of England's page daily. 1 credit. Use this to work out what a late invoice is owed; for how a named company pays its suppliers use payment_practices or will_they_pay.

paid.description: The date it was paid; leave out if unpaid

tools.name: will_they_pay
tools.description: A large customer's payment habits from the supplier's side, with what its lateness is worth on your invoice. From the company's statutory Payment Practices reports - typical days to pay against your terms, the share paid late and past 60 days, the trend over its last reports - and the statutory interest plus fixed compensation its typical lateness is worth on an invoice of your size. A company that doesn't report is said so. 1 credit. Use this when you supply (or are quoting) the company and want the cost on your invoice; for the plain record and its benchmark use payment_practices.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: sponsor_licence
tools.description: Is an organisation on the register of licensed sponsors (workers), on which routes and at what rating. Matched on the organisation's name as the register writes it (a company number brings its registered and former names), with the register's town checked against the registered office. Current licences, former licences with the date they went, and every change recorded for the name since 6 October 2026. 1 credit. Use this for the Home Office register of licensed worker sponsors; for other registers use registers, aml_register, sra_check or cqc_check.

company.description: A company number, or the organisation's name

tools.name: deadlines
tools.description: Every deadline a UK company has, sorted, with days left. Accounts and confirmation statement (Companies House), each director's and PSC's identity-verification date as counts (the earliest among those not yet showing as verified), the ICO data protection fee renewal (the fee register entry matching the company's name), and the next payment practices and gender pay gap reports where the company reports them. Overdue first. The reply carries the address of a free calendar feed for the company. 1 credit. Use this for what is due and when; for the filings themselves use accounts or public_record.

company.description: A company number, or a name

tools.name: contracts_won
tools.description: Public-sector contracts a UK company has been awarded. From Contracts Finder and Find a Tender award notices — count, notified value (contracts and framework ceilings apart; `contracts.withoutValue` counts awards with no published value), top buyers and the latest awards (the lots of one notice as one line with `lots`; a notice published on both feeds once, the other under `alsoNotified`). Matched by company number where a notice gives one (both feeds' numbers read since 10 Oct 2026), else by exact registered name. 1 credit. Use this for public-sector awards the company has won; public_record carries a summary of the same.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: gender_pay_gap
tools.description: An employer's gender pay gap reports, read and benchmarked. Median and mean gaps, bonus gaps, women by pay quarter, year-on-year trend and rank against all reporters and the sector. 1 credit. Only employers with 250 or more staff must report, so a smaller one usually has none; public_record carries a summary of the same.

company.description: A UK company number (such as 00502851) is surest; an employer's name also works and the reply names the employer it matched.

tools.name: registers
tools.description: Environment Agency registrations and a UK Sanctions List check for one company. Waste carrier / broker / dealer status and expiry, permits, exemptions and enforcement actions (England), plus whether the company's number, name or former names match an entity on the UK Sanctions List (a lead to confirm, never a finding). 2 credits. Use this for environmental permits and a sanctions screen; for other registers use aml_register, sra_check, cqc_check, charity_check or sponsor_licence.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: distress_signals
tools.description: What the Companies House register shows about a company's health. Status, strike-off proposals, insolvency cases, overdue filings, recent charges and directors leaving — each graded serious / watch / info with a date, plus a one-line summary. A name resolves to one company first. 1 credit. Use this for a quick health check; for the filed figures use accounts, for a fuller picture public_record.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.

tools.name: payment_practices
tools.description: How fast a large UK company pays its suppliers. From the company's statutory Payment Practices reports (OGL v3) — average days to pay, share paid late against agreed terms, terms, trend over its last reports, benchmark against all recent reporters, and a plain reading for suppliers. 1 credit. A name also returns otherMatches (other reporting companies it matches, by number). Use this for the payment record itself and its benchmark; for what the lateness is worth on your own invoice use will_they_pay, and for the PPN 018 and Fair Payment Code tests use ppn_018.

company.description: A UK company number (8 characters, such as 00502851 or SC123456) is surest; a name also works and goes to the closest registered company, which the reply names. Use company_search first when a name could mean several companies.
